## Research Question

Where are forest-fire events concentrated within Ketapang Regency, and how does their spatial distribution and interaction change across the observed 2026 period, particularly as the dry season progresses.

## Study Area and Data

- Study area: Ketapang Regency, West Kalimantan, Indonesia
- Fire data: NASA FIRMS, VIIRS S-NPP + NOAA-20, 1 Jan - 11 Sept 2026
- Boundary data: indonesia-geospasial.com (DUKCAPIL 2019)
- 51,205 fire points after cleaning

## Data Preparation Summary

- Combined archive + NRT data from both satellites
- Filtered to Ketapang boundary, reprojected to UTM 49S
- 0 duplicates, 0 empty geometries, 0 missing coordinates
- Dropped 2,803 low-confidence detections (\~5.2%)

## First-Order Findings

- KDE (Diggle bandwidth, 239m) shows persistent hotspots in western Ketapang
- Quadrat test rejects spatial randomness (p \< 2.2e-16)
- Fire activity intensified sharply Aug-Sep (93% of all detections)

## Second-Order Findings

- G, F, K, L functions all confirm clustering vs CSR
- Clustering persists across all tested distances up to 5km
- No sign of clustering effect weakening within tested range

## Value-Added Analysis

- Compared K-function across Pre-escalation, Onset, Crisis phases
- Pre-escalation phase shows higher intensity-normalised clustering than Crisis
- Suggests different fire origin patterns between quiet and crisis periods

## Integrated Interpretation

Fires concentrate in specific areas, intensify sharply during the dry season, and show genuine spatial clustering rather than random occurrence - with clustering character differing between quiet and crisis periods.

## Limitations

- Low-confidence detections excluded (\~5.2% of data)
- K/L functions bounded to 5km; true clustering scale not fully captured
- VIIRS detection limitations (cloud/smoke cover, \~375m resolution)
- Boundary dataset is from 2019
- Observation period covers partial year only

## Public-Safety Implications

- Hotspot areas can prioritise monitoring and rapid-response resources
- Jul-Aug window is critical for pre-positioning resources
- Differentiated response: targeted early-season intervention vs broad crisis-phase containment
- Findings describe pattern, not cause - land-use data needed for full risk model

## References

NASA FIRMS (2026). VIIRS S-NPP and NOAA-20 Active Fire Data, Ketapang Regency.

Indonesia Geospasial (2019). Batas Administrasi Kabupaten/Kota Tahun 2019 (DUKCAPIL).

Spatial Point Patterns: Methodology and Applications with R.
